facts.raw_span: asymptomatic cutaneous lesions on the face that had progressively spread to the trunk and extremities
asthenia and mild intermittent arthralgias
Multiple millimetric erythematous to hyperpigmented monomorphic keratotic papules involving the head, trunk, and extremities
Symmetric annular brown erythematous plaques on the cheeks and temples
No vesicles or pustules
Normal white blood cell count
Mild anemia (hemoglobin level, 11.3 g/dL; normal level 12.50-15.50 g/dL)
Hypocomplementemia
Moderate proteinuria
Raised levels of antinuclear antibodies (>1:160)
Positive: anti-Smith antibodies, SSA/Ro antibodies, SSB/La antibodies, and anti-U1RNP antibodies
Slightly atrophic epidermis with interface dermatitis, individual dyskeratotic keratinocytes, and a superficial perivascular and interstitial infiltrate of neutrophils

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of cutaneous lesions, asthenia, and arthralgias, along with laboratory findings of mild anemia, hypocomplementemia, and positive anti-Smith antibodies, are consistent with Subacute Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus.
The patient's symptoms of asthenia, arthralgias, and laboratory findings of mild anemia, hypocomplementemia, and positive anti-Smith antibodies, are consistent with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
The patient's symptoms of cutaneous lesions, specifically the millimetric erythematous to hyperpigmented monomorphic keratotic papules, are consistent with Discoid Lupus Erythematosus.
The patient's symptoms of asthenia, arthralgias, and laboratory findings of mild anemia, hypocomplementemia, and positive anti-U1RNP antibodies, are consistent with Mixed Connective Tissue Disease.
The patient's symptoms of cutaneous lesions, specifically the symmetric annular brown erythematous plaques, are consistent with Cutaneous Leukocytoclastic Vasculitis.
The patient's laboratory finding of mild anemia is consistent with Anemia of Chronic Disease.
The patient's laboratory finding of moderate proteinuria is consistent with Nephrotic Syndrome.
The patient's laboratory finding of mild anemia is consistent with Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia.
The patient's laboratory findings of moderate proteinuria and raised levels of antinuclear antibodies are consistent with Lupus Nephritis.
The patient's symptom of arthralgias is consistent with Rheumatoid Arthritis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation of asymptomatic cutaneous lesions, symmetric annular brown erythematous plaques, and laboratory findings such as mild anemia, moderate proteinuria, and raised levels of antinuclear antibodies are most consistent with Subacute Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus. The presence of specific autoantibodies like anti-Smith, SSA/Ro, and SSB/La antibodies further supports this diagnosis.
